newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps all head southwards, bar Brent CFDs.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps all head southwards, bar Brent CFDs.

text.p: European oil swaps fell on Wednesday except Brent CFDs, which began fairly steady then took a lead from weaker screen crude which has been pressured lower by a wave of selling.
Levels had been fairly steady until the mid-afternoon.
News that Iraqi oil sales under the U.N. "oil-for-food" deal would not begin until money currently held in an escrow account was spent, was bullish but not sufficiently so.
Gasoline dropped $4, naphtha was off $2.50 and heavy fuel shed over $1.
Brent CFDs were fairly thinly traded with June 23-27 assessed around -32 cents against August, June 30-4 at -34 cents and July 7-11 at -33 cents.

Dealers said June 23-27 traded at -32 cents against August and also at -30 cents earlier in the morning. June 23-27 traded in the morning versus July 14-18 at -4 cents and July 14-18 traded versus July 21-25 at -5 cents.
Heavy fuel saw several deals with $83, $83.25 and $82 all heard done on July and $85 done twice on September. Further out 3Q97 went at $84 and 4Q97 was pegged at $90.50 with 1Q98 put at $93.50.
Med swaps traded at $75.50 for July and $76.00 for August.

Gasoline swaps ran out of steam dropping about $4.00 a tonne. with July trading at $81.50, $82.50 and $83.50 compared with values of $187 on Tuesday. Dealers said August was heard offered $82.25 with bids about 50 cents below July bids. Most of the activity was around 1600-1700 GMT, after the market assessed the direction of NYMEX.
Naphtha tracked crude lower with July slipping to $176.50 with August and September showing only minimal contangoes in the order of 50 cents and $1 respectively.
